findings.title: Cash advance fee
findings.triggered_by: Cash Advance Fee $5.00 or2.00% of the amount of each cash advance, whichever is greater (Maximum Fee:$500.00)
findings.search_query_used: credit card cash advance fee percentage minimum

precedents.case_name: Livingston v. Fast Cash USA, Inc.
In re Capital One Bank Credit Card Interest Rate Litigation

findings.plain_language_explanation: This card charges you $5 or 2% (whichever is more) every time you get cash from an ATM or cash advance. These fees add up fast on top of interest.
findings.user_impact: With irregular income, cash advances seem tempting but will cost you $5-500 each time you need cash.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: You need $200 cash for rent. The fee is $5, plus high interest starts immediately. If you can't pay it back quickly, you'll owe much more than you borrowed.

recommended_actions.action: Avoid cash advances entirely - use debit card or bank ATM instead
Set up automatic payments to avoid late fees that lead to cash advance needs

findings.title: Late payment fee
findings.search_query_used: credit card late payment fee maximum amount

precedents.case_name: Thelma Perry v. First National Bank, Doing Business as First National Credit Card

findings.plain_language_explanation: This credit card charges up to $25 every time you pay late. Even paying one day after the due date triggers this fee.
findings.user_impact: With irregular gig income and late payment history, you'll likely face frequent $25 fees.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: Missing 3-4 payments yearly could cost $75-100 in late fees alone. Combined with your irregular income, this could trap you in a cycle of debt and more late payments.

recommended_actions.action: Set up automatic minimum payments from your bank account to avoid late fees
recommended_actions.contact: Your bank or credit card company

recommended_actions.action: Look for credit cards with no late fees or lower penalty rates for gig workers

findings.title: Returned payment fee
findings.search_query_used: credit card returned payment fee NSF bounce
findings.plain_language_explanation: You'll pay up to $25 every time a payment bounces because you don't have enough money in your account when they try to collect.
findings.user_impact: With irregular income, you could face multiple $25 fees that pile up quickly.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: Your gig income varies month to month. If payments bounce 3 times in one month, you'd owe $75 in fees alone - possibly more than your actual payment amount.

recommended_actions.action: Set up account alerts to warn you before payments are due
recommended_actions.contact: Your bank's customer service or mobile app

recommended_actions.action: Ask the creditor about payment date flexibility to match your income schedule
Consider switching to a credit union with lower or no returned payment fees
recommended_actions.contact: Local credit unions in your area

findings.title: Pay-by-phone fee
findings.search_query_used: credit card phone payment fee charge
findings.plain_language_explanation: This company charges you $10 every time you pay your bill by phone. This fee applies even if you use automated phone systems.
findings.user_impact: With irregular income, you may need to pay by phone more often, costing $120+ per year.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: Given your late payment history and irregular income, you'll likely need phone payments during tight months. At $10 each time, this could cost $120-240 yearly.

recommended_actions.action: Set up free automatic online payments or find free payment methods before signing
Ask company to waive phone fees for low-income customers

findings.title: Statement copy fee
findings.search_query_used: credit card statement copy fee per page
findings.plain_language_explanation: The company charges $5 for each page of old statements you request. This can add up fast if you need multiple pages or statements.
findings.user_impact: With irregular income, unexpected $5-per-page fees could strain your budget when you need records.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: Needing 6 months of statements for a loan application could cost $30-60. With your income situation, this fee could delay important financial decisions or applications.

recommended_actions.contact: Your bank's customer service or website

recommended_actions.action: Ask if the bank waives statement fees for customers with payment difficulties

findings.title: Broad collateral securing credit card debt
findings.triggered_by: Credit extended under this credit card account is secured by various personal property and money including, but not limited to: (a) any goods you purchase with this account, (b) any shares you specifically pledge as collateral for this account on a separate Pledge of Shares, (c) all shares you have in any individual or jointaccount withtheCreditUnion excluding sharesinanIndividual RetirementAccount orinanyotheraccount that would lose special tax treatment under state or federal law, and (d) collateral securing other loans you have with the Credit Union excluding dwellings.
findings.description: Broad cross-collateralization gives creditor rights to seize multiple unrelated assets for credit card debt
findings.search_query_used: credit extended under this credit card account secured credit card consumer rights
findings.plain_language_explanation: This credit card uses everything you buy with it AND your bank shares as collateral. If you can't pay, they can take those items back.
findings.user_impact: With irregular income and late payments, you risk losing purchases and bank shares if you fall behind.
findings.estimated_risk_scenario: Miss payments due to gig work income gaps, lose items you bought plus any shares you have with this bank. Creates bigger financial hole than typical credit cards.

recommended_actions.action: Find unsecured credit cards instead - they can't take your property if you default
If you must use this card, never charge essential items you can't afford to lose
Build emergency fund for irregular income before taking secured debt
